name: Somalia: al-Shabaab insurgency and political crisis
started: 2025-02-01 (approximate; al-Shabaab offensive in central Somalia and federal political breakdown)
summary: Al-Shabaab, al-Qaeda's Somali affiliate, has retaken ground in central and southern Somalia while the federal government is consumed by disputes with member states and the opposition over the president's expired term. US commanders have publicly tied al-Shabaab's gains to those political fights.

sides.name: Federal Government of Somalia and partners
backers: United States (air strikes, special forces; aid suspended to the federal government in Jan 2026)
Egypt (troops, helicopters and aircraft in AUSSOM from early 2026)
leaders: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud (President; mandate expired 15 May 2026 and is disputed)
sides.strength: AUSSOM agreed strength 11,900 (Uganda 4,500, Ethiopia 2,500, Djibouti 1,520, Kenya 1,410, Egypt 1,091), per Wikipedia.

sides.name: Al-Shabaab
backers: Houthis (reported weapons smuggling via Eritrea and Sudan, per CTP)
sides.strength: No current figure found in the sources reviewed.

background: Al-Shabaab has fought Somali governments and African Union forces since 2006 and still controls much of the rural south and centre, taxing trade and running courts. A government offensive in 2022 and 2023 pushed it out of parts of Hiraan and Middle Shabelle, but it regained ground from early 2025.

The federal model is under strain: Puntland and Jubaland refuse to recognize federal authority, the opposition Somali Future Council rejects the president's plan for direct elections, and Israel's recognition of Somaliland in December 2025 added a new dispute. That matters because troops and attention diverted to political fights are not fighting al-Shabaab.
year: Al-Shabaab attacked Godka Jilicow prison in Mogadishu on 4 October 2025. On 26 December Israel recognized Somaliland. In January 2026 the US suspended assistance to the federal government over alleged food aid theft, and Somalia revoked its agreements with the UAE. In March South West State cut ties with Mogadishu, and federal forces took Baidoa on 30 March and installed a transitional administration; loyalist militias later attacked Baidoa and Buurhakaba. Talks with the opposition collapsed on 15 May as the president's term expired, and Puntland declared federal mandates over. On 3 and 4 June government forces fought armed supporters of opposition leaders, including former prime minister Hassan Ali Khaire and former president Sheikh Sharif, in Mogadishu's Howlwadaag district ahead of an anti-government rally, with mortar fire and deaths reported by the UN. On 1 July the US said it would end all funding for the UN Support Office in Somalia, the roughly $500 million a year logistics system behind AUSSOM, by 31 December 2026. In late July AFRICOM's commander warned that political disputes had let al-Shabaab retake cleared areas, and on 2 August al-Shabaab seized Teedaan in eastern Hiiraan after a nearly 24-hour battle, taking control of a road linking Hiiraan with Galgaduud and Middle Shabelle. The US kept up a record air campaign: about 125 strikes in 2025 and 68 by late June 2026. Piracy resurged from April, with at least eight hijackings.
situation: As of October 2026 al-Shabaab holds most of the rural Juba valley and contests Middle and Lower Shabelle and Hiraan, where it took Teedaan in August. The federal government faces a legitimacy dispute, armed standoffs with South West loyalists and the opposition, and an AUSSOM mission that ACLED says faces 'imminent operational collapse' in 2027 unless the US funding cut is replaced. Somalia has aligned with Egypt and Eritrea in the El Alamein bloc while also offering Ethiopia port access.
technical: AUSSOM replaced ATMIS on 1 Jan 2025 under UN Security Council Resolution 2767; Uganda is the largest contributor with about 4,500 troops along the corridor into Mogadishu.
Egypt deployed troops plus attack and utility helicopters and light fixed-wing aircraft in early 2026.

US posture: AFRICOM denied a withdrawal was under consideration (late July 2026), and US special operations signed a deal with Puntland on 2 Aug 2026 to expand the Bosaso base for counterterrorism and maritime security.
Houthi weapons smuggling to al-Shabaab and ISIS-Somalia via Eritrea and Sudan has been reported (CTP).
Piracy resurgence from April 2026: at least eight vessels hijacked, versus one from 2014 to 2022.
Federal forces took Baidoa on 30 Mar 2026 without reported casualties, but loyalists of ousted South West leader Abdiaziz Laftagareen later attacked Baidoa and Buurhakaba.

US air campaign: about 125 AFRICOM strikes in 2025, double the previous record of 63 in 2019, after a directive from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave commanders more authority; 68 strikes in 2026 by 22 June (Stars and Stripes). New America's monthly tally for 2026: January 26, February 16, March 7, April 12, May 2.
Turkish air support: Somalia's defence ministry said joint Somali-Turkish strikes killed 35 al-Shabaab fighters at hideouts and weapons stores in Lower Shabelle (30 Jun 2026; claim unverified).

Funding cliff: the US will end support for the UN Support Office in Somalia (about $500 million a year) by 31 Dec 2026; ACLED expects al-Shabaab to exploit the 2026 to 2027 transition and threaten Mogadishu and Kismayo.
Teedaan (2 Aug 2026): al-Shabaab claimed weapons, vehicles and equipment after government forces and clan militias withdrew; it then dug trenches in the village.
Opposition leaders accuse the president of using internationally trained counter-al-Shabaab units against them in Mogadishu (June 2026).
casualties: No reliable 12-month total was found in the sources reviewed. The 'high' label reflects the long-running scale of the insurgency, record US and Somali air strikes and continuing ground battles, and should be checked against ACLED data.
displaced: No current figure found in the sources reviewed.

timeline.event: Al-Shabaab attacks Godka Jilicow prison in Mogadishu.
US suspends assistance to the federal government.
Somalia revokes all bilateral agreements with the UAE.
South West State cuts ties with Mogadishu.
Talks with the Somali Future Council collapse as the president's term expires.
Two days of fighting in Mogadishu between government forces and armed supporters of opposition leaders.
US announces it will end funding for the UN Support Office in Somalia by year-end.
Al-Shabaab seizes Teedaan in eastern Hiiraan; US and Puntland sign agreement to expand the Bosaso base.
Somalia joins the El Alamein declaration with Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan.

outlook: Watch whether the government and opposition agree an election path, whether AUSSOM funding survives into 2027, and whether al-Shabaab presses toward Mogadishu's outskirts while federal forces are split.

battles.name: Battle of Teedaan
battles.place: Teedaan, eastern Hiiraan, Somalia (approx; exact site unverified)
sides: Somali government forces and clan militias
battles.outcome: Al-Shabaab took the village after nearly 24 hours of fighting; government forces withdrew and set up positions on the outskirts.
battles.forces: Al-Shabaab assault force; Somali army and local militias.
battles.losses: Both sides took casualties per locals; no figures. Al-Shabaab claimed captured weapons and vehicles.
battles.significance: Controls a road linking Hiiraan with Galgaduud and Middle Shabelle that al-Shabaab can use to move and tax traffic; came days after AFRICOM warned of reversals.

battles.name: Mogadishu clashes between government and opposition forces
sides: Federal security forces, police and NISA
Armed supporters of opposition leaders (Hassan Ali Khaire, Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed)
battles.outcome: Fighting around an arms-recovery raid on Khaire's residence ahead of an anti-government rally; the intelligence agency director mediated a halt.
battles.forces: Government security forces against opposition-aligned gunmen; mortar shells hit several buildings.
battles.losses: No official figures; the UN Secretary-General said the violence caused deaths and civilian injuries.
battles.significance: Armed confrontation in the capital over the president's disputed term, which US commanders link to al-Shabaab's battlefield gains.

sources.label: AP via News4Jax: Armed clashes erupt in Somalia's capital

battles.name: Federal takeover of Baidoa
sides: South West State administration of Abdiaziz Laftagareen
battles.outcome: Federal forces took the state capital; Laftagareen was forced out and a transitional head installed. Loyalist militias later attacked Baidoa and Buurhakaba.
battles.losses: No casualties reported for the takeover itself.
battles.significance: Federal use of force against a member state, diverting troops from the fight against al-Shabaab.
